examples.problem_statement: Solve the system: Equation (1): $x + y + z = 4$; Equation (2): $2x - y + 3z = 13$; Equation (3): $3x - 2y - 2z = 2$

solution.result: \begin{aligned}x + y + z = 4 \quad \text{(1)} \\ 2x - y + z = 12 \quad \text{(2)} \\ x + 2y - z = -9 \quad \text{(3)}\end{aligned}
solution.description: Identify the three linear equations with three unknowns to solve.

solution.operation: Eliminate z by adding equations (1) and (3)
solution.description: Adding equations (1) and (3) cancels z since +z and -z are additive inverses.
Combine like terms: x + x = 2x, y + 2y = 3y, z - z = 0, and 4 - 9 = -5.

solution.operation: Eliminate z by adding equations (2) and (3)
solution.description: Adding equations (2) and (3) also cancels z, giving a second equation in x and y only.
Combine like terms: 2x + x = 3x, -y + 2y = y, z - z = 0, and 12 - 9 = 3.
Isolate y to prepare for substitution into equation (4).
Replace y with (3 - 3x) to create an equation in one variable x.
Distribute, combine like terms, and isolate x by dividing both sides by -7.

solution.operation: Find y by substituting x = 2 into equation (6)
solution.description: Substitute the known value of x back into the expression for y.

solution.operation: Find z by substituting x = 2 and y = -3 into equation (1)
solution.description: Use the original equation (1) to find z by substituting the known values of x and y.

examples.problem_statement: Solve the equation $x^2 + x - 6 = 0$ by factorization

solution.description: Match the equation to the standard form a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero and read off the coefficients a = 1, b = 1 and c = -6.

solution.operation: Find factors of $ac$ that add to $b$
solution.description: Multiply a by c to get -6; this is the product the factor pair must hit, while their sum must match b = 1.
Test the factor pairs of -6 and find that 3 and -2 work, since 3 times -2 is -6 and 3 plus -2 is 1.
Split the single middle term x into 3x minus 2x using the pair just found; the equation is unchanged but is now ready for grouping.
Bracket the four terms into two pairs, chosen so that each pair has a common factor.
Take x out of the first bracket and -2 out of the second, leaving the identical binomial x + 3 inside both groups.
Because x + 3 is common to both terms, factor it out and the quadratic becomes a product of two brackets.
A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero, so set each bracket equal to zero in turn.
Solve the two short linear equations to obtain the roots x = 2 and x = -3.

examples.answer: The roots of $x^2 + x - 6 = 0$ are $x = -3$ and $x = 2$.

examples.problem_statement: Solve the equation $x^2 + 2x - 8 = 0$ by factorization

solution.operation: The factors of $x^2$ are $x$ and $x$. These are placed in brackets: $(x\ )(x\ )$
solution.description: Start the trial-and-error method: x squared can only be written as x times x, so open two brackets each beginning with x.

solution.operation: The factors of $-8$ are $+8$ and $-1$, or $-8$ and $+1$, or $+4$ and $-2$, or $-4$ and $+2$.
solution.description: List every integer pair whose product is -8, since the second entries of the two brackets must multiply to the constant term.

solution.operation: The only combination to give a middle term of $+2x$ is $+4$ and $-2$.
solution.description: Test each pair against the required middle term and keep only +4 and -2, the pair whose cross products add to +2x.
Write the completed factorisation, so the quadratic becomes the product of x + 4 and x - 2.

solution.operation: (Note that the product of the two inner terms ($4x$) added to the product of the two outer terms ($-2x$) must equal the middle term, $+2x$ in this case.)
solution.description: Check the choice: the inner product 4x added to the outer product -2x gives 2x, which matches the middle term of the original equation.

Losing a sign when splitting the middle term, writing x squared plus 3x plus 2x minus 6 instead of 3x minus 2x.

examples.problem_statement: Solve $2x^2 + 5x = 3$ by completing the square

solution.operation: Write the equation in standard form
solution.description: Bring the 3 across so all terms sit on one side, giving the standard form needed before completing the square.

solution.operation: Divide all terms by coefficient of x²
solution.description: Divide every term by 2 so the x squared term has coefficient 1, which the completing-the-square procedure requires.

solution.operation: Move constant term to right side
solution.description: Move the constant three halves to the right, leaving only the x squared and x terms on the left.

solution.operation: Complete the square: add square of half the coefficient of x
solution.description: Take half of the x coefficient five halves to get five quarters, square it, and add that same amount to both sides so the equation stays balanced.
The left side is now the perfect square of x plus five quarters; on the right, add three halves and twenty-five sixteenths over the common denominator 16 to get forty-nine sixteenths.

solution.operation: Take square root of both sides
solution.description: Undo the square by taking the square root of both sides, keeping both signs, since the square root of forty-nine sixteenths is plus or minus seven quarters.
Subtract five quarters from both sides so x stands alone, still carrying the plus-or-minus.
Separate the plus case from the minus case to obtain the two roots, one half and negative three.

examples.answer: x = 0.5 or x = -3; i.e., the roots of the equation $2x^2 + 5x = 3$ are 0.5 and $-3$.

examples.problem_statement: The area of a rectangle is 23.6 cm^2 and its width is 3.10 cm shorter than its length. Determine the dimensions of the rectangle, correct to 3 significant figures.

solution.description: Name the two unknowns before anything else: l for the length in centimetres and w for the width in centimetres.

solution.operation: Express width in terms of length
solution.description: Translate the phrase width is 3.10 cm shorter than the length into the relation w = l - 3.10.
Write the area relationship for a rectangle: length times width equals the given 23.6 square centimetres.
Replace w by l - 3.10 so the area equation contains the single unknown l.

solution.operation: Expand and rearrange to standard quadratic form
solution.description: Multiply out the bracket and move 23.6 across, producing the standard quadratic l squared minus 3.10 l minus 23.6 equals zero.
Apply the quadratic formula, minus b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4ac, all over 2a, with a = 1, b = -3.10 and c = -23.6.
Evaluate the discriminant: 9.61 plus 94.4 is 104.01, whose square root is about 10.1985.
Work out both branches of the plus-or-minus, giving lengths of about 6.649 cm and about -3.549 cm.
A length cannot be negative, so discard -3.549, round 6.649 to 6.65 cm to three significant figures, and subtract 3.10 to get the width 3.55 cm.
Check the answer against the given data: 6.65 times 3.55 is 23.6075, which is 23.6 square centimetres to three significant figures.

examples.problem_statement: Calculate the diameter of a solid cylinder which has a height of 82.0 cm and a total surface area of 2.0 m^2.

Substitute the known height and total surface area into that formula and rearrange so the radius appears as a squared term.
Tidy the coefficients into the standard quadratic form in the radius r, ready for the formula.
Solve that quadratic for r, keeping only the positive root since a radius cannot be negative.
Double the radius to obtain the diameter, 0.5748 m, which is 57.5 cm.

examples.problem_statement: Determine the values of x and y which simultaneously satisfy the equations y = 5x - 4 - 2x^2 and y = 6x - 7

solution.description: Both expressions are equal to y, so set them equal to each other; the x-values that satisfy this are where the line meets the curve.

solution.operation: Move all terms to left side
solution.description: Subtract 6x and add 7 to both sides so every term is on the left and the right side is zero.
Collect like terms: 5x minus 6x leaves -x, and -4 plus 7 leaves 3.
Multiply every term by -1 so the leading coefficient becomes positive, which makes the quadratic easier to factor.
Factor by finding two numbers with product 2 times -3, that is -6, and sum 1, namely 3 and -2; this gives the brackets 2x + 3 and x - 1.
A product is zero only if one factor is zero, so set each bracket equal to zero.
Solve the two short linear equations to get the x-values -3/2 and 1.
Substitute x = -3/2 into the simpler equation y = 6x - 7, giving y = -16.
Substitute x = 1 into the same linear equation, giving y = -1.
Put both pairs, (-3/2, -16) and (1, -1), back into the original curve and line equations to confirm each satisfies both.

examples.problem_statement: Write (a) log 30 (b) log 450 in terms of log 2, log 3 and log 5 to any base

solution.description: Split 30 into its prime factors 2, 3 and 5, the only numbers the answer is allowed to contain.
Recall the first law of logarithms, that the logarithm of a product is the sum of the logarithms.

solution.operation: Write log 30 in terms of prime factors
solution.description: Apply that law to the prime factorisation, so log 30 becomes log 2 plus log 3 plus log 5.
Factorise 450 the same way, as 2 times 3 squared times 5 squared.
Recall the third law, that the logarithm of a power is the exponent times the logarithm.
Write log 450 as the logarithm of that prime factorisation, ready for both laws.
Use the product law to split the three factors and the power law to bring the exponents down, giving log 2 plus 2 log 3 plus 2 log 5.

examples.answer: log 30 = log 2 + log 3 + log 5; log 450 = log 2 + 2 log 3 + 2 log 5

examples.problem_statement: Write log((8 × ⁴√5)/81) in terms of log 2, log 3 and log 5 to any base

solution.operation: log((8 × ⁴√5)/81) = log 8 + log ⁴√5 − log 81
solution.description: Separate the expression with the product and quotient laws: the two factors on top become a sum of logarithms and the 81 underneath becomes a subtraction.
Rewrite each number as a power of a prime, so 8 is 2 cubed, the fourth root of 5 is 5 to the power one quarter, and 81 is 3 to the fourth.
Bring each exponent down in front of its logarithm with the power law, giving 3 log 2 plus one quarter log 5 minus 4 log 3.

examples.problem_statement: Evaluate (log 25 − log 125 + (1/2) log 625)/(3 log 5)

solution.operation: log 25 − log 125 + (1/2) log 625 = log 5² − log 5³ + (1/2) log 5⁴
solution.description: Write every number in the numerator as a power of 5: 25 is 5 squared, 125 is 5 cubed and 625 is 5 to the fourth.
Bring those exponents down with the power law and collect the coefficients, since 2 minus 3 plus 2 leaves a single log 5.
The numerator is now 1 log 5 over the denominator 3 log 5, so the common factor log 5 cancels top and bottom.
What remains is the plain number one third.

examples.problem_statement: Solve the equation log(x − 1) + log(x + 8) = 2 log(x + 2)

solution.description: Combine the two logarithms on the left with the product law into a single logarithm of the product of x - 1 and x + 8.
Multiply that product out, so the left side is the logarithm of x squared plus 7x minus 8.
On the right, use the power law in reverse to turn 2 log of x + 2 into the logarithm of x + 2 all squared.
Expand the square, so the right side is the logarithm of x squared plus 4x plus 4.
Each side is now a single logarithm to the same base, so the two can be set equal.
Equal logarithms to the same base force equal arguments, so drop the logarithms and equate the two quadratics.
The x squared terms are identical on both sides and cancel, leaving a linear equation.
Collect the x terms on one side and the numbers on the other to reach 3x = 12.
Divide by 3 to get x = 4, which keeps x - 1, x + 8 and x + 2 all positive, so the solution is valid.

examples.problem_statement: Solve the equation (1/2) log 4 = log x

solution.description: Use the power law to move the coefficient one half up as an exponent, turning half of log 4 into the logarithm of 4 to the power one half.
A power of one half is a square root, so this is the logarithm of the square root of 4.

solution.operation: Hence, (1/2) log 4 = log x becomes log √4 = log x
solution.description: Replace the left-hand side of the equation with that single logarithm.
The square root of 4 is 2, so the equation now reads log 2 equals log x.
Equal logarithms to the same base mean equal arguments, so 2 equals x.

solution.operation: i.e. the solution of the equation is x = 2
solution.description: State the result the other way round: the solution of the equation is x = 2.
